stories.title: How I Met Your Mother — Episode 1: Infatuation
stories.topic: Dad tells Maya how he met Mom — Rohan and Elena, a Meridian Soft trip to the Bay Area, nights around the Grand Oriole Hotel.

panels.scene_description: Living-room sofa at night, soft lamp. Dad sits beside Maya — no book — knees almost touching. Maya grins sideways; Dad already looks doomed.
panels.dialogue:
Maya: Okay. Spill. How did you actually meet Mom?
Dad: ...You sure you want the full version? It's embarrassing.
Maya: Perfect. I live for your embarrassment.
panels.caption: PRESENT · Living room · after dinner

panels.scene_description: Close two-shot: Dad rubs the back of his neck; Maya leans in sparkling.
panels.dialogue:
Dad: Fine. Spring, years ago. Company sent me to the Bay Area office for two weeks.
Maya: 'Two weeks' is always how these movies start. Continue, tragic hero.
panels.caption: PRESENT · Living room

panels.scene_description: Elegant title card: bay dusk skyline, tiny tram lights, soft feather motif.
panels.caption: HOW I MET YOUR MOTHER · Episode 1 — Infatuation

panels.scene_description: Young Rohan exits arrivals with suitcase; California light hits curly hair. Tiny nervous sparkles around his eyes — excited and out of place.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): First Saturday I landed — jetlagged, pretending I knew what I was doing.
panels.caption: SATURDAY · March 8 · San Jose Airport · ~9:00 AM

panels.scene_description: Hotel corridor: Rohan, Kabir, Arjun compare apartment listing screens; comic shock at rents.
panels.dialogue:
Kabir: Bro, this rent can't be real.
Arjun: It is. Welcome to California math.
Rohan: We need a flat. And also... sleep.
panels.caption: SATURDAY · March 8 · Grand Oriole Hotel corridor · afternoon

panels.scene_description: Sunday: Rohan alone on hotel bed staring at ceiling; boredom lines; phone idle.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): Sunday I was so bored I went downstairs just to walk in circles like a professional circle-walker.
panels.caption: SUNDAY · March 9 · Hotel room · late morning

panels.scene_description: Lobby panorama — time slows. Across the space: Elena in Meridian Soft tee, tall, baby-cut brunette, pretty — looking at her phone. Rohan freezes mid-step.
panels.dialogue:
Dad (V.O.): That was the first time I saw her face.
Maya (inset): Mom in a company tee? Immediate legend status.
panels.caption: SUNDAY · March 9 · Grand Oriole Lobby · ~11:20 AM

panels.scene_description: Extreme close-up of Rohan's eyes reflecting Elena; tiny butterflies hatch around his temples.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): Curly-hair IT guy brain: short-circuit. Pretty. Tall. Same company shirt. Dangerous combination.
panels.caption: SUNDAY · March 9 · Lobby · internal beat

panels.scene_description: Rohan introduces himself awkwardly; Elena gives a cool reserved glance — could be shy or cold.
panels.dialogue:
Rohan: Hi— uh— same company? I'm Rohan. Meridian Soft...
Elena: Elena.
Dad (V.O.): That look. Condescending? Or did I invent it because pretty girls scramble me?
panels.caption: SUNDAY · March 9 · Lobby

panels.scene_description: Present: Maya covers mouth laughing; Dad covers face with both hands.
panels.dialogue:
Maya: You disliked her AND liked her? Multitasking!
Dad: Don't put that on a poster.
Maya: Mental billboard. High resolution.
panels.caption: PRESENT · Living room

panels.scene_description: Monday curb: Wei's car; Rohan Kabir Arjun pile in; Wei confident at wheel.
panels.dialogue:
Wei: Hop in. Office express.
Rohan: Wei, you are the hero of mornings.
panels.caption: MONDAY · March 10 · Hotel curb · ~8:15 AM

panels.scene_description: Tuesday transit stop alone: no Wei. Soft wind. Destiny ripple lines around Rohan's shoes.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): Tuesday — Wei couldn't drive us. A tiny change. Destiny wears casual clothes.
panels.caption: TUESDAY · March 11 · City light-rail stop · ~8:05 AM

panels.scene_description: Platform: Elena in white-and-blue with a pretty hat — morning light turns cinematic. Rohan's pupils widen; sparkles.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): And there she was again. White and blue. That hat. I forgot how to be a person.
panels.caption: TUESDAY · March 11 · Light-rail platform

panels.scene_description: Tram interior: Rohan manages a tiny intro then becomes a statue; silence drawn as comic panels between them.
panels.dialogue:
Rohan: Hi... again. Rohan.
Elena: Morning.
Dad (V.O.): Then — silence. Olympic silence. My mouth filed a resignation letter.
panels.caption: TUESDAY · March 11 · Light rail · morning commute

panels.scene_description: Present: Maya freezes face like statue Rohan; Dad groans.
panels.dialogue:
Maya: Strategy: exist silently near crush.
Dad: It was... presence.
Maya: It was cowardice with good hair.
panels.caption: PRESENT

panels.scene_description: Office day-one montage: Marcus handshake, badge scan, laptop — Rohan sweaty but trying.
panels.dialogue:
Marcus: Welcome aboard, Rohan. Lunch later?
Rohan: Thank you, sir— I mean Marcus— I mean— okay.
panels.caption: TUESDAY · March 11 · Meridian Soft Bay Campus · daytime

panels.scene_description: Wednesday lobby: both wait for rideshare; quiet stretches like elastic; Rohan's hands fidget.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): Wednesday. Lobby again. Same quiet. Saying 'hi' felt like climbing a mountain in flip-flops.
panels.caption: WEDNESDAY · March 12 · Hotel lobby · morning

panels.scene_description: Cafeteria: Marcus waves; Rohan arrives late with tray; table full — soft panic.
panels.dialogue:
Marcus: Rohan! We saved— wait, we filled up.
Dad (V.O.): Late again. Destiny... or bad cafeteria timing. Same thing that week.
panels.caption: WEDNESDAY · March 12 · Office cafeteria · lunch

panels.scene_description: Rohan sits across Elena alone at small table — soft spotlight between trays.
panels.dialogue:
Rohan: Mind if I sit? We keep... existing near each other in lobbies.
Elena: Sure.
panels.caption: WEDNESDAY · March 12 · Cafeteria · lunch

panels.scene_description: Talk beat: Rohan animated with hands about California smiling culture; Elena listening, faint smile blooming.
panels.dialogue:
Rohan: People here smile at strangers like it's a sport.
Elena: You're new. Give it a week.
Rohan: A week of smiling — or panicking?
panels.caption: WEDNESDAY · March 12 · Cafeteria

panels.scene_description: Feeling close-up: Rohan watching her listen more than talk — manhwa soft focus on her lashes.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): She listened more than she spoke. I liked that. Quiet isn't empty — sometimes it's careful.
panels.caption: WEDNESDAY · March 12 · Cafeteria · mid-lunch

panels.scene_description: Evening curb: Elena enters cab alone; Wei's text about flat hunt. Rohan torn silhouette.
panels.dialogue:
Dad (V.O.): Wei left early for apartments. She rode alone. I told myself it was fine.
Maya (inset): Your face is lying to Future You.
panels.caption: WEDNESDAY · March 12 · Office curb · evening

panels.scene_description: Thursday dinner: Rohan alone at hotel restaurant — introvert fortress with phone.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): Thursday I sat alone. Not because I disliked people — because girls, even platonically, scrambled my confidence.
panels.caption: THURSDAY · March 13 · Hotel dining lobby · ~7:10 PM

panels.scene_description: Elena sits opposite unexpectedly — electric crackle doodles; Rohan jolts; butterflies explode.
panels.dialogue:
Elena: Hi.
Rohan: —!
Dad (V.O.): She sat across from me. My heart rebooted incorrectly.
panels.caption: THURSDAY · March 13 · Hotel dining · evening

panels.scene_description: Present: Maya making zap sound effects with fingers; Dad smiling helplessly.
panels.dialogue:
Maya: BZZT. Crush.exe has crashed.
Dad: It crashed into a better version of me.
panels.caption: PRESENT

panels.scene_description: Long dinner montage feeling: plates emptier, clocks melt ~2 hours, laughter lines, eyes soft.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): Two hours. Work. Random things. Easy and terrifying — like learning to swim mid-ocean.
panels.caption: THURSDAY · March 13 · Hotel dining · ~7:10–9:10 PM

panels.scene_description: Night street walk under lamps; Elena gestures keep walking; Rohan would walk forever.
panels.dialogue:
Elena: One more block?
Rohan: Okay.
Elena: ...Okay one more?
Dad (V.O.): She kept insisting we walk. I would've walked to Oregon.
panels.caption: THURSDAY · March 13 · Downtown streets · night

panels.scene_description: Walk feeling panel: sideways glance — is this friendship? His fingers twitch near hers and retreat.
panels.dialogue:
Rohan (thought): Don't read too much. Don't read too little. Why is there no manual?
Dad (V.O.): I wanted to know how girls think — and somehow the answer was walking beside one.
panels.caption: THURSDAY · March 13 · Night walk

panels.scene_description: Hotel hallway: Rohan bursts into friends' room gushing; Kabir Arjun Wei roast him.
panels.dialogue:
Rohan: Guys. There's a girl.
Kabir: There are many girls.
Rohan: No — a girl girl.
Arjun: Oh no. He's gone.
Wei: Destiny hours.
panels.caption: THURSDAY · March 13 · Friends' hotel room · ~11:20 PM

panels.scene_description: Rohan asleep peaceful; phone lights with Elena's follow request — unseen. Dramatic irony sparkles.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): Slept like a baby at midnight. Phone got a follow request... and I — genius — had deleted the app a year ago.
panels.caption: THURSDAY night → FRIDAY · 12:00 AM · Hotel room

panels.scene_description: Present: Maya facepalms so hard the couch shakes.
panels.dialogue:
Maya: You DELETED the app?
Dad: I was living pure. Offline. Philosophical.
Maya: You were living romantic stupid. Cute stupid, but stupid.
panels.caption: PRESENT

panels.scene_description: Friday afternoon: Rohan glowing while getting ready; phone shows Elena invite to club Friday eve.
panels.dialogue:
Elena (text): Club tonight? Friends going — come!
Rohan (text): Yes!! Excited to meet everyone!
Dad (V.O.): I got ready like it was a wedding. Heart doing cartwheels.
panels.caption: FRIDAY · March 14 · Afternoon → evening · Hotel room

panels.scene_description: Phone close-up: later text — too many people, maybe skip. Rohan's face cracks; little dark rain.
panels.dialogue:
Elena (text): Actually... lots of people. Maybe skip tonight?
Dad (V.O.): Cancelled. Upset. Almost angry. Thumb hovered over delete contact.
panels.caption: FRIDAY · March 14 · Evening · Hotel room

panels.scene_description: Present careful: Dad softer; Maya quieter but still herself.
panels.dialogue:
Dad: Then I criticized myself. Acquaintance — not entitled to her Friday.
Maya: Grown-up Dad speaking. Rare form.
Dad: I performed grown-up by lying I was 'busy' the next day.
panels.caption: PRESENT

panels.scene_description: Saturday day: Rohan with Arjun walking 'fine'; thought bubbles of Elena cancelled club.
panels.dialogue:
Arjun: You okay?
Rohan: Busy. Very busy. Busy with busy-ness.
Arjun: ...You're upset.
panels.caption: SATURDAY · March 15 · Day · city sidewalk

panels.scene_description: Saturday hotel dining lobby: Elena approaches Rohan + Arjun; apologetic soft eyes.
panels.dialogue:
Elena: Rohan — I'm sorry about last night. Can I make it up?
Rohan: Uh— this is Arjun.
Arjun: Hi. Friendly obstacle. Nice to meet you.
panels.caption: SATURDAY · March 15 · Hotel dining lobby · evening

panels.scene_description: Movie invite; Rohan asks Arjun; Arjun declines with subtle wink away from Elena.
panels.dialogue:
Elena: Theater nearby — want to watch something?
Rohan: Arjun, you in?
Arjun: Busy. Deeply busy. Ancient busy. You two go... as friends.
panels.caption: SATURDAY · March 15 · Lobby

panels.scene_description: Rohan scrolling to invite Kabir/Wei; Elena gently places hand on his phone — softness zoom.
panels.dialogue:
Rohan: Wait I can ping Kabir—
Elena: No need.
Dad (V.O.): Hand on my phone. Brain typed FRIENDS. Destiny typed DATE??
panels.caption: SATURDAY · March 15 · Lobby

panels.scene_description: Present roast panel — Maya pointing at imaginary whiteboard labeled 'HINTS YOU MISSED'.
panels.dialogue:
Maya: Mom said 'no need' and you still held a friendship press conference?
Dad: Allergic to implications.
Maya: Get an epipen for romance.
panels.caption: PRESENT

panels.scene_description: Hallway: Rohan invents tiredness; Elena reads him; invites movie in her room — just us.
panels.dialogue:
Rohan: I'm tired. Sleep. Definitely sleep.
Elena: What are you actually going to do?
Rohan: ...Watch a movie.
Elena: Then watch in my room. Just us.
panels.caption: SATURDAY · March 15 · Hotel hallway · ~9:40 PM

panels.scene_description: Rohan in his room grabbing iPad Pro — freeze-frame terror, sweat drops, butterfly storm.
panels.dialogue:
Dad (V.O.): Best part — I was terrified.
Maya (present): Of Mom?
Dad: Of accidentally becoming a person who sits on a bed near a crush.
panels.caption: SATURDAY · March 15 · Rohan's room

panels.scene_description: Elena's room: Rohan plants iPad on desk far away like a professional; Elena points to bed.
panels.dialogue:
Rohan: Desk is good. Cinema of professionalism.
Elena: Bed's better. Come on.
panels.caption: SATURDAY · March 15 · Elena's hotel room · night

panels.scene_description: On bed edge plugging charger; Elena scoots closer for the screen — distance collapses; butterflies fill room air.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): She came closer so she could see. I froze. Every butterfly in California moved into my stomach.
panels.caption: SATURDAY night · Elena's room

panels.scene_description: Watching soft-horror Night Watchman: jump scare; Elena jolts closer, almost head on shoulder; water bottle; comic stomach growl bubbles.
panels.dialogue:
SFX: JUMP!
Elena: —!
Dad (V.O.): Every scare: closer. Almost her head on my shoulder. She drank water like dinner forgot her. Her stomach growled. Weirdly adorable.
panels.caption: SATURDAY night · ~10:30 PM–1:00 AM · Elena's room · movie: Night Watchman

panels.scene_description: Rohan thought storm overlay: hints? friendship? romance? manhwa question-mark rain.
panels.dialogue:
Rohan (thought): Is she giving hints?
Am I failing Hint Class?
Is this friendship with jump scares?
Dad (V.O.): Confused. Crushed. Still sitting like a gentleman statue.
panels.caption: SATURDAY night · Elena's room · internal

panels.scene_description: Present: Maya whispering like gossip show host.
panels.dialogue:
Maya: Head. Nearly. On. Shoulder.
Dad: I know.
Maya: And you did... statues?
Dad: Elite statues.
panels.caption: PRESENT

panels.scene_description: 2AM Rohan returns; can't sleep; 4AM text from Elena can't sleep either — soft phone glow.
panels.dialogue:
Elena (text, 4:01 AM): Still awake. That movie ruined me.
Dad (V.O.): Woke at seven, saw it, and thought — wait. Maybe...?
panels.caption: SUNDAY · March 16 · 2:00 AM → 4:01 AM → 7:00 AM

panels.scene_description: Flat hunting till 1PM with friends; Elena excited movie texts overlay between rental disasters.
panels.dialogue:
Kabir: This closet is pretending to be a bedroom.
Elena (text): Still on for movie later??
Rohan (text): YES.
panels.caption: SUNDAY · March 16 · Morning–1:00 PM · apartment search

panels.scene_description: Walking to Silverleaf Mall theater in sun — side by side; soft cinematic widen.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): Walked to the theater. The whole afternoon felt like a scene someone wrote for me.
panels.caption: SUNDAY · March 16 · ~3:00 PM · Silverleaf Mall approach

panels.scene_description: Starbucks: tissue falls; both dive; forehead bump; shared smile — spark line through Rohan's stomach.
panels.dialogue:
SFX: bonk
Elena: Ow—
Rohan: Sorry—!
Both: ...
Dad (V.O.): That smile went straight through my stomach.
panels.caption: SUNDAY · March 16 · Starbucks · pre-movie

panels.scene_description: Present: Maya softens, hand over heart dramatically.
panels.dialogue:
Maya: Okay that was illegally cute.
Dad: Right? I still replay the head-bonk in 4K.
panels.caption: PRESENT

panels.scene_description: Dark theater: sitting close; Rohan's hand hovers near hers — almost — retreats.
panels.dialogue:
Dad (V.O.): In the dark: Do I put my hand on hers?
Maya (present): Dad. The answer was yes.
Dad: I know that NOW.
panels.caption: SUNDAY · March 16 · Cinema · afternoon showing

panels.scene_description: Outside theater: Rohan asks for social; Elena already sent; gentle roast energy.
panels.dialogue:
Rohan: Can I get your... social?
Elena: I already sent it. Days ago.
Rohan: I deleted the app. Philosophically.
Elena: Reinstall philosophy, Rohan.
panels.caption: SUNDAY · March 16 · Theater plaza · late afternoon

panels.scene_description: Evening montage: dinner, walk, second movie in her room — 'best day' stamp glowing.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): Dinner. Walk. Another movie in her room. Best day of the trip. Felt like a date... even while I refused the word.
panels.caption: SUNDAY · March 16 · Evening → night

panels.scene_description: Monday campus: lunch together, hallway waves between breaks — unlabeled couple energy.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): Monday — breaks, lunch, leave together, dinner, walk. A ritual was forming.
panels.caption: MONDAY · March 17 · Campus + hotel · day–evening

panels.scene_description: Hotel room: watching Rohan's pick — soft Indian romantic Roja vibes (tasteful); warm scenes → they glance at each other then look away.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): Alternate-day rule. My choice: Roja. When warm scenes came... we looked. Silently. Then pretended the wall was fascinating.
panels.caption: MONDAY · March 17 · Night · Elena's room

panels.scene_description: Graphic: hotel checkout countdown as a ticking heart calendar.
panels.caption: COUNTDOWN · Rohan checks out Thu morning (Mar 20) · Elena Fri (Mar 21)

panels.scene_description: Present: Maya counting on fingers.
panels.dialogue:
Maya: So your brain: movies good / labeling feelings bad.
Dad: Accurate. Painfully accurate.
panels.caption: PRESENT

panels.scene_description: Tuesday: Rohan can't work; friends huddle advice — ask her clear.
panels.dialogue:
Kabir: Ask. Friend or more.
Wei: Clear is kind.
Arjun: Or die of confusion — also popular.
Rohan: If I ask, it might get awkward forever.
panels.caption: TUESDAY · March 18 · Office break area · daytime

panels.scene_description: Rohan at desk staring at code he cannot see — Elena silhouette in thoughts.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): Whole day unproductive. Heart louder than keyboard.
panels.caption: TUESDAY · March 18 · Desk · daytime

panels.scene_description: Tuesday night Forrest Gump glow; comfortable until phone rings.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): Night. Her movie — Forrest Gump. Beautiful. Then her brother called.
panels.caption: TUESDAY · March 18 · ~9:30 PM · Elena's room

panels.scene_description: Elena on phone lies 'lots of friends' while Rohan alone beside her — hurt then courage rising.
panels.dialogue:
Elena (on phone): Yeah, just hanging out with a bunch of friends.
Dad (V.O.): I was the only bunch. That lie opened a door. Honesty walked through.
panels.caption: TUESDAY · March 18 · During call

panels.scene_description: After call: Rohan gentle confrontation — last movie as friends vs long future of movies.
panels.dialogue:
Rohan: Why did you lie?
Elena: ...
Rohan: Hey — this might be our last movie as friends... or the start of movies together for a long, long future.
panels.caption: TUESDAY · March 18 · After call

panels.scene_description: Elena shocked: wasn't interested at first; Rohan sad awkward; gut still whispers she cares.
panels.dialogue:
Elena: I wasn't interested in you at first.
Rohan: ...Oh.
Dad (V.O.): Sad. Awkward. Gut still whispered she cared.
panels.caption: TUESDAY · March 18 · Elena's room

panels.scene_description: She says get out; he stays, takes her hand, kneels sincerely — earnest not wedding parody.
panels.dialogue:
Elena: Get out first.
Rohan: I won't. Please hear me.
Dad (V.O.): I took her hand. Knelt — not for theater. For truth.
panels.caption: TUESDAY · March 18 · Elena's room

panels.scene_description: Elena: scared of dating after friends' heartbreaks; Rohan: we pull each other up when we fight.
panels.dialogue:
Elena: I'm scared. I've watched friends shatter.
Rohan: Breakups happen when people stop pulling each other up. If we fight, we pull. We learn each other. Accept me — for dating.
panels.caption: TUESDAY · March 18 · Elena's room

panels.scene_description: Close-up: Rohan names LIMBO DATE — manhwa title-card energy on the phrase.
panels.dialogue:
Rohan: Call it a Limbo Date. Not nothing. Not everything. The honest middle — tell me how you really feel.
Elena: ...Limbo Date?
panels.caption: TUESDAY · March 18 · Elena's room

panels.scene_description: Elena admits little interest but too early; Rohan: better early than late; answer by tomorrow dinner.
panels.dialogue:
Elena: I had a little interest... but it felt too early.
Rohan: Better early than late. Bad at flirting. Good at honesty. Think tonight. Tell me at tomorrow's dinner.
panels.caption: TUESDAY · March 18 · Late

panels.scene_description: Awkward hallway exit; Elena alone conflicted on bed; Rohan's silhouette walking away small.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): Left awkwardly — like a man who put his heart on the carpet and hoped nobody stepped on it.
panels.caption: TUESDAY · March 18 · Hallway / her room · late

panels.scene_description: Present: Maya wiped-eyed still roasting.
panels.dialogue:
Maya: You KNEELED?
Dad: Respectfully!
Maya: Mom must've thought you were proposing to the carpet.
Dad: ...Possibly.
panels.caption: PRESENT

panels.scene_description: Wednesday: Elena WFH; empty office chair; Rohan restless pacing thoughts.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): She didn't come to campus. Worked from hotel. I respected space. My stomach did not.
panels.caption: WEDNESDAY · March 19 · Office daytime

panels.scene_description: Dinner: Elena careful — stay in contact, don't talk about yesterday; Rohan happy but senses uneven footing.
panels.dialogue:
Elena: Let's stay in contact. But please — not last night's talk. Not tonight.
Rohan: Okay. I can do that.
Dad (V.O.): Happy. She looked careful. Something unfinished.
panels.caption: WEDNESDAY · March 19 · Hotel dining · evening

panels.scene_description: Night walk: Forrest Gump feather / opportunity speech; Elena soft-shocked.
panels.dialogue:
Rohan: Forrest Gump — that feather. Great relationships are like opportunity. They float by. I didn't want to waste it. That's why I asked early.
Elena: ...You remembered that?
Dad (V.O.): Soft-shocked. The good kind.
panels.caption: WEDNESDAY · March 19 · Night walk near hotel

panels.scene_description: Movie night different energy — knowing glances; truth in the room; quiet victory smiles.
panels.dialogue: Dad (V.O.): Movie as usual. Different. The truth sat between us. Phase one — honesty — somehow worked. I was solitary... but willing to understand.
panels.caption: WEDNESDAY · March 19 · Night · Elena's room

panels.scene_description: Present close: Maya leans head on Dad's shoulder; both soft lamp-lit.
panels.dialogue:
Dad: Lots happened after that...
Maya: Part Two. Tomorrow. Non-negotiable. Bring snacks for my emotional damage.
Dad: Deal.
panels.caption: PRESENT · Living room · late

panels.scene_description: End card: white feather drifting through warm hotel hallway; To Be Continued.
panels.caption: END OF EPISODE 1 — INFATUATION · TO BE CONTINUED IN PART 2

stories.title: The Cockroach Janta Party: When Students Ask for Fair Exams
stories.topic: How the CJP student protest started (test episode)

panels.scene_description: Dad and Daughter at bedtime, cozy room with soft lamplight. Dad sits on the edge of the bed, holding a picture book, while Daughter snuggles under a warm blanket with curious eyes.
panels.dialogue:
Dad: 'Tonight, beta, I want to tell you a true story about brave young people in India who asked for something fair. Are you ready?'

Daughter: 'Yes, Papa! I love true stories.'
panels.caption: A bedtime tale begins: A father tells his daughter about courage and fairness.

panels.scene_description: Dad gestures kindly while explaining. A thought-bubble shows many Indian students sitting at desks with large exam papers, looking nervous and hopeful.
panels.dialogue:
Dad: 'You know, in India there are very big, important tests called entrance exams. Millions of students take them to get into good colleges.'

Daughter: 'That sounds really hard, Papa.'
panels.caption: Understanding the challenge: Many students compete in entrance exams across India.

panels.scene_description: Dad's face becomes gentle but serious. Another thought-bubble shows worried families reading news on phones and newspapers about exam problems.
panels.dialogue:
Dad: 'But one day, something troubling happened. News said some exam papers had leaked out before the test. Families felt the system wasn't being fair.'

Daughter: 'Oh no! That's not right, Papa!'
panels.caption: When fairness breaks: News of exam irregularities worries students and families.

panels.scene_description: Dad's eyes light up warmly. In the thought-bubble, a young man (Abhijeet Dipke) steps off a plane or arrives with a determined, kind expression.
panels.dialogue: Dad: 'Then, a brave young man named Abhijeet Dipke, who had been studying in America, came back to India. He thought: "We must ask our leaders to fix this!"'
panels.caption: A young leader returns: Abhijeet Dipke comes back to help students.

panels.scene_description: Thought-bubble shows Abhijeet speaking kindly to a small gathering of students, explaining his idea. Students nod and listen intently.
panels.dialogue:
Abhijeet (in thought-bubble): 'Let's bring students together peacefully and ask for fairness. We'll ask leaders to listen to us.'

Dad (narrating): 'And the students said: "Yes, we will speak up!"'
panels.caption: A spark of courage: Abhijeet gathers students to organize peacefully.

panels.scene_description: Thought-bubble shows a beautiful, famous landmark—Jantar Mantar in Delhi—surrounded by hundreds of peaceful students holding signs about fair exams. The signs are clear and kind: 'Fair Exams for All,' 'Listen to Students,' 'Fairness Now.'
panels.dialogue: Dad (narrating): 'Soon, students gathered at a famous place in Delhi called Jantar Mantar. They came together peacefully, with signs and kind voices asking for fairness.'
panels.caption: Voices rise: Students gather peacefully at Jantar Mantar to ask for fair exams.

panels.scene_description: Dad leans in with a warm, knowing smile. A thought-bubble shows the students with a funny, silly name written on some signs: 'Cockroach Janta Party.' Students are smiling—it's a bit of gentle humor amid seriousness.
panels.dialogue:
Dad: 'Now here's something funny, beta. The students called their movement the "Cockroach Janta Party"—or CJP. Do you know why?'

Daughter: 'Why, Papa?'
panels.caption: A funny, clever name: Students use satire to show they are ordinary people.

panels.scene_description: Dad smiles warmly, explaining. A thought-bubble shows ordinary everyday scenes: a shopkeeper, a farmer, students, a teacher—all kinds of regular people.
panels.dialogue:
Dad: 'Because "Janta" means ordinary people—like shopkeepers, farmers, and students. They were saying: "We are not fancy politicians. We are normal people asking for fairness!"'

Daughter: 'Oh! I like that, Papa.'
panels.caption: Janta means people: The movement spoke for everyone who wanted fairness.

panels.scene_description: Thought-bubble shows Prime Minister Modi in formal attire, in his office, receiving reports about the students' concerns. He listens respectfully. Nearby, Amit Shah, the Home Minister, is also shown reading about the protests.
panels.dialogue: Dad (narrating): 'When Prime Minister Modi and the government leaders heard what the students were asking, they listened. Leaders have a responsibility to hear what people care about.'
panels.caption: Leaders listen: The Prime Minister and government hear the students' voices.

panels.scene_description: A thought-bubble shows the Education Minister at a desk with papers about exam reforms, looking thoughtful and focused on improving the system.
panels.dialogue: Dad (narrating): 'The Education Ministry began looking at how to make exams more fair and secure. They knew students deserved honesty and trust.'
panels.caption: Working toward change: The government addresses student concerns about exam integrity.

panels.scene_description: Thought-bubble shows students celebrating gently—not with wild parties, but with quiet pride. Some are back at their studies, looking more hopeful. Others are speaking to younger students about fairness.
panels.dialogue: Dad (narrating): 'The students learned something important: when you speak peacefully about what's right, people listen. Change takes time, but it begins with courage.'
panels.caption: A lesson in speaking up: Students discover the power of peaceful voices.

panels.scene_description: Dad and Daughter are back in the cozy bedroom. Dad closes the storybook gently while Daughter snuggles deeper into blankets, eyes growing sleepy and content. Stars twinkle outside the window.
panels.dialogue:
Dad: 'And so, beta, remember: fairness matters. When you see something unfair, you can speak up kindly and bravely. The world listens to gentle, strong voices.'

Daughter: 'I will, Papa. Thank you for the story.' (yawns softly)

Dad: 'Sleep well, my dear. Dream of a fair and kind India.'
panels.caption: Sweet dreams: A father and daughter rest, knowing that fairness begins with courage.

stories.title: Et tu, Brute? How a Republic Dies
stories.topic: Et tu, Brute? — Julius Caesar and the fragile Roman Republic

panels.scene_description: Nighttime bedroom, warm lamp. Dad sits on the edge of the bed, daughter cross-legged with a thick history book open to a map of Rome.
panels.dialogue:
Daughter: 'Et tu, Brute?' Dad, was Brutus a hero or a traitor?
Dad: That question has outlived him by two thousand years. Tonight we watch a republic die - slowly, then all at once.
panels.caption: Rome, before the emperors. A state built so no single man could rule it all.

panels.scene_description: Dad gestures; behind him a faded vision of the Roman Forum with togaed figures voting and arguing.
panels.dialogue:
Dad: The Republic shared power - elected officials, a Senate, popular assemblies. They'd thrown out their kings and swore: never again one master.
Daughter: So it was like... a democracy with rules?
panels.caption: Res Publica - 'the public thing.' Power on loan, never owned.

panels.scene_description: Battlefield flashback: Caesar in crimson-edged toga over armor, standing tall, laurel light around him, legions behind.
panels.dialogue:
Caesar: I gave Rome Gaul, order, and glory. Let the timid Senate debate while I win. History thanks the strong hand, not the slow committee.
Roman People: Caesar! Caesar feeds us! Caesar wins!
panels.caption: Caesar (I): Rome bled for a century. I am the cure it is too proud to swallow.

panels.scene_description: Wide river at dawn; Caesar on horseback at the water's edge, army waiting, Senate scroll trampled in mud.
panels.dialogue: Caesar: The Senate orders me to disband my army and come home powerless. I cross this river instead.
panels.caption: 49 BCE. The Rubicon. A general brings his private army against his own state. There is no crossing back.

panels.scene_description: Split panel: on one side a triumph parade with banners of Caesar's face; on the other, senators in shadow watching uneasily.
panels.dialogue:
Roman People: Dictator for life! Long life to Caesar!
Senate: Banners with one man's face. Statues. 'For life.' We fought kings for this?
panels.caption: Victory made him beloved - and permanent. Dictator perpetuo. To some, freedom. To others, a crown by another name.

panels.scene_description: Daughter interrupts, pointing at the book; Dad half-turned.
panels.dialogue:
Daughter: But the people LOVED him. If they voted for him, isn't that democracy?
Dad: Careful. A crowd cheering one man is not the same as a people keeping their rules. That's the whole trap.
panels.caption: Dad: Popularity can hollow out a republic from the inside - with applause.

panels.scene_description: Dim colonnade. Cassius, lean and sharp, grips Brutus's arm; Brutus looks tormented.
panels.dialogue:
Cassius: While we talk of laws, he becomes a god with an army. I need a name Rome trusts. I need you, Brutus.
Brutus: You mix Rome's freedom with your own grudges, Cassius.
panels.caption: Cassius (I): Ideals are lovely. But someone must count the swords. Brutus is the noble face the people will forgive.

panels.scene_description: Brutus alone, moonlight, holding a small bust of an ancestor; conflict on his face.
panels.dialogue: Brutus: I love Caesar the man. But I love the Republic more than any man. If one Roman may become king, then no Roman is free.
panels.caption: Brutus (I): Not from hate. From duty. Rome must outlive her heroes - even the one I call friend.

panels.scene_description: Calpurnia at a window at dawn, clutching Caesar's cloak, storm outside; Caesar dressing to leave.
panels.dialogue:
Calpurnia: I dreamed your blood on the marble. Stay home today. Please.
Caesar: If I hide from every whisper of fear, I am not Caesar. The Senate waits.
panels.caption: Calpurnia: Power costs the house first. I am the fear he cannot afford to hear.

panels.scene_description: Interior of the Theatre of Pompey's Curia. Caesar enters among senators; conspirators drift closer, hands hidden in togas.
panels.dialogue:
Senate: A petition, Caesar - just here, come closer.
Caesar: Speak, then. I have a Rome to govern.
panels.caption: The Ides of March, 44 BCE. They meet in Pompey's hall - the Senate house was under repair. The circle closes.

panels.scene_description: Stark shock beat: silhouette of the crowd of daggers rising against a bright window; Caesar's shadow buckling. No gore, high contrast.
panels.dialogue:
Caesar: You too, Brutus?
Brutus: For Rome, old friend. For Rome.
panels.caption: The wound was in the body of one man - and in the body of the state.

panels.scene_description: Brutus stands over the aftermath (off-panel body), raising a bloodless hand to a stunned, silent Senate. Doubt flickers.
panels.dialogue:
Brutus: Romans! The tyrant is dead - the Republic lives again! Rejoice!
Senate: ...silence.
panels.caption: Brutus (II): I assumed they'd cheer liberty. That was my blindest wound of all.

panels.scene_description: The Forum. Antony in a vivid red cloak before a vast crowd, gesturing at Caesar's covered bier, tears becoming fire.
panels.dialogue:
Antony: They call themselves honorable men. Look - he left his gardens to YOU, the people. Is THIS your reward to him?
Roman People: Traitors! Burn the murderers' houses!
panels.caption: Antony: Their daggers had reasons. I have his cloak, his will, and your grief. Watch which one moves a crowd.

panels.scene_description: Montage of chaos: conspirators fleeing Rome, armies massing, smoke over the city.
panels.dialogue:
Cassius: We killed the man and multiplied the war. The crowd never wanted a republic. It wanted a father.
Brutus: What have we freed, Cassius? Only more knives.
panels.caption: No liberty returned. Only civil war - and soon, an emperor named Augustus to end all doubt.

panels.scene_description: Back in the bedroom, daughter frowning at the book, Dad watching her think.
panels.dialogue:
Daughter: So Brutus wasn't a hero OR a traitor. He was... wrong about people.
Dad: He thought one dagger could restart freedom. Freedom isn't a machine you reset by killing a man. Political violence usually just opens the next war.
panels.caption: The strongman fell. The Republic did not rise. That gap is the lesson.

panels.scene_description: Dad closes the book gently; daughter looks resolved. Faint modern city skyline reflected in the window behind them.
panels.dialogue:
Dad: Watch for the pattern, not the toga: banners with one face, 'for the people' from every mouth, rules bent for a winner everyone loves.
Daughter: So freedom isn't the hero. It's... us staying awake.
Dad: And the institutions we refuse to hollow out. Heroes and knives don't save republics. Awake citizens do.
panels.caption: Rome fell into empire not in one stab, but in a thousand cheers. Democracies die when we stop guarding the rules - and stay saved when we don't.

stories.title: The Hitler Warning: How Hate Captured a Democracy
stories.topic: Hitler, propaganda, and how democracy can die — teen warning episode

panels.scene_description: Night study. A history book open between them. The lesson is a warning, not a spectacle.
panels.dialogue:
dad: Tonight we study how a democracy can be talked into dying—and how propaganda turns neighbors into targets.
daughter: Dad… how do ordinary people become bystanders? Could a pattern like that happen again?
panels.caption: Night study. A history book open between them. The lesson is a warning, not a spectacle.

panels.scene_description: Early 1930s Germany: unemployment lines, worthless savings stories, and politicians selling rage as strength.
panels.dialogue:
weimar_citizen: Prices, jobs, shame after the war… maybe a hard fist will save us.
dad: Pain was real. The demagogue’s medicine was a lie: blame minorities instead of rebuilding justice.
panels.caption: Early 1930s Germany: unemployment lines, worthless savings stories, and politicians selling rage as strength.

panels.scene_description: Hitler sells a fake story of national rebirth built on racial hierarchy and conspiracy fantasies.
panels.dialogue:
adolf_hitler: Democracy is weak. Follow one will. Remove the 'poison' I name—and Germany rises.
dad: Listen carefully: racial hatred and genocide ideology are evil and false. Scapegoating Jews and other minorities never 'heals' a country.
panels.caption: Hitler sells a fake story of national rebirth built on racial hierarchy and conspiracy fantasies.

panels.scene_description: Daughter names the trick before it hardens into 'common sense.'
panels.dialogue:
daughter: So he speaks for 'the people' while planning to strip people’s rights?
dad: Exactly. Authoritarians borrow the word 'people' to erase persons. That is the warning.
panels.caption: Daughter names the trick before it hardens into 'common sense.'

panels.scene_description: 1933: appointed Chancellor; emergency powers and the Enabling Act hollow out the republic. Opposition vanishes into prisons and camps.
panels.dialogue:
adolf_hitler: We’ll use the law—then the law will kneel.
dad: Dictatorship can walk in through legal doors if courts, parties, and citizens stop defending pluralism.
panels.caption: 1933: appointed Chancellor; emergency powers and the Enabling Act hollow out the republic. Opposition vanishes into prisons and camps.

panels.scene_description: Gleichschaltung: press, radio, film, and schools pulled into one loud story. Book burnings teach fear of questions.
panels.dialogue:
joseph_goebbels: Repeat the lie until it feels familiar. Fill every speaker and classroom. Make doubt look traitorous.
daughter: That’s not debate—that’s drowning people so they can’t hear truth.
panels.caption: Gleichschaltung: press, radio, film, and schools pulled into one loud story. Book burnings teach fear of questions.

panels.scene_description: Dad maps the craft to modern pattern language—without inventing private crimes about living leaders.
panels.dialogue:
dad: Same gears today: coordinated hate memes, rumor floods, and media ecosystems that reward outrage against immigrants or minorities.
daughter: So social media can become a modern Forum if we share before we check?
dad: Yes. Propaganda trains reflexes. Literacy slows the reflex.
panels.caption: Dad maps the craft to modern pattern language—without inventing private crimes about living leaders.

panels.scene_description: Nuremberg Laws: citizenship and dignity cut away with paperwork and badges of exclusion.
panels.dialogue:
anne_frank_symbol: Yesterday I was a classmate. Today a law says I am less than a neighbor.
german_neighbor: …I don’t want trouble.
panels.caption: Nuremberg Laws: citizenship and dignity cut away with paperwork and badges of exclusion.

panels.scene_description: Kristallnacht: broken glass in the street—public violence taught as normal.
panels.dialogue:
dad: When windows shatter and people cheer or shrug, democracy’s moral backbone is already cracking.
anne_frank_symbol: Please—see me. Not a rumor. A person.
panels.caption: Kristallnacht: broken glass in the street—public violence taught as normal.

panels.scene_description: Terror as policy: secret police, camps for opponents, a racial-purity cult wearing uniforms of order.
panels.dialogue:
heinrich_himmler: Fear will organize the nation. Purity is the excuse; the boot is the method.
dad: A police state is not 'safety.' It is power without mercy—and it always needs an internal enemy.
panels.caption: Terror as policy: secret police, camps for opponents, a racial-purity cult wearing uniforms of order.

panels.scene_description: War accelerates genocide. Deportations become timetables. Murder hides inside logistics language.
panels.dialogue:
adolf_eichmann: Trains, lists, quotas. I don’t decide—I deliver. Orders are orders.
daughter: That’s still choosing. Paperwork doesn’t wash blood off a decision.
panels.caption: War accelerates genocide. Deportations become timetables. Murder hides inside logistics language.

panels.scene_description: Dad names the history Hannah Arendt later helped the world confront: the banality of evil.
panels.dialogue:
dad: Six million Jews were murdered in the Holocaust—among millions of other victims. Industry and bureaucracy made cruelty efficient.
anne_frank_symbol: We were not numbers first. We had birthdays. Jokes. Future plans.
panels.caption: Dad names the history Hannah Arendt later helped the world confront: the banality of evil.

panels.scene_description: A White Rose echo: students risk everything so truth can still circulate in the dark.
panels.dialogue:
resistance_voice: Silence is a choice. Truth is worth the risk—pass it on.
joseph_goebbels: Crush the leaflets. Call courage 'treason.'
panels.caption: A White Rose echo: students risk everything so truth can still circulate in the dark.

panels.scene_description: Aftermath classroom: institutions matter—and so do habits of courage.
panels.dialogue:
dad: Never again is a verb: protect minorities, defend a free press, keep courts independent, and vote against strongman shortcuts after economic fear.
daughter: And refuse the sentence 'not my business' when a classmate is mocked as less human.
panels.caption: Aftermath classroom: institutions matter—and so do habits of courage.

panels.scene_description: They translate history into present civic radar—patterns, not conspiracy fan-fiction about living politicians.
panels.dialogue:
daughter: When leaders praise 'order' while attacking free reporters… when memes smear immigrants as an infestation… I should hear the 1930s echo.
dad: Yes. Ask: Who is being dehumanized? Who benefits if we stop checking facts? Democracy dies of neglected alarms.
panels.caption: They translate history into present civic radar—patterns, not conspiracy fan-fiction about living politicians.

panels.scene_description: Close the book—not the duty.
panels.dialogue:
daughter: I won’t be a bystander. If hate targets a minority, I speak, I check sources, I stand with them.
dad: That’s the Hitler warning: refuse the lie, protect your neighbors, guard votes and a free press—so genocide ideology finds no open door.
panels.caption: Close the book—not the duty.
